prompt:
Write 6 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a hit while turning left claim, in time order. Injury: wrist fracture. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1086; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- It is not yet clear whether the injury came from this crash.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- The patient was treated for the same body area within the last two years, and that condition adds to the current complaints.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim reported by the insured's policyholder after a collision at an intersection where the vehicle was turning left and was struck on the driver side. The claimant is represented by counsel, and all further contact will be routed through the attorney's office. The driver is named on the policy, and the policy was in force at the time of loss.

Entry 2: Reviewed the police report and spoke with the responding officer, who confirmed the claimant was in the vehicle at the scene. No independent witnesses have come forward, so the account rests on the parties involved and the photographs taken at the scene. The photos confirm some of the details reported by the claimant.

Entry 3: Vehicle inspection completed. The damage is mostly consistent with the impact described by all parties. No prior damage to the vehicle is known, and nothing in the file suggests the damage predates the start of coverage.

Entry 4: The claimant has given the same account in every conversation so far, including the initial statement and the follow-up call. The wrist fracture claimed is still under review, and it is not yet clear whether the injury resulted from this crash. Medical records show the claimant was treated for the same body area within the last two years, and that prior condition appears to add to the current complaints.

Entry 5: Received medical billing and treatment notes. Treatment followed a usual course for this type of injury and tapered off as the patient improved. Records have been requested from the treating providers to clarify the timeline of the prior condition relative to this loss.

Entry 6: File remains open pending receipt of the requested medical records and the attorney's demand package. Next review scheduled once those documents are received and the causation question has been assessed.
